name: Mobile Application Security (Android & iOS)
tagline: Testing your own or authorized Android & iOS apps: static analysis, decompilation, runtime instrumentation, traffic interception, emulators, and CTF practice grounds.

tools.name: jadx
tools.desc: One-step DEX-to-Java decompiler (CLI and GUI) that rebuilds readable Java source, resources, and AndroidManifest.xml into a searchable project view.
tools.when: Default first pass on a fresh APK you are authorized to test: navigate the reconstructed project and follow flows across classes.
tools.install: Download the latest zip from GitHub releases (or brew install jadx)

tools.name: jadx-gui
tools.desc: The graphical frontend bundled with jadx for interactive cross-referencing, renaming obfuscated identifiers, and exporting decompiled selections.
tools.when: Interactive exploration and annotation when reading a flat decompile is not enough and you want quick class-to-class navigation.
tools.install: Launch the gui main class from the jadx release zip (or brew install jadx)

tools.name: apktool
tools.desc: Decodes resources and AndroidManifest.xml into editable form and exposes smali/baksmali bytecode, then rebuilds the APK for repackaging tests.
tools.when: Edit res/ or smali and repackage the APK for behavior/repackage checks on apps you are authorized to modify.
tools.install: Download the jar wrapper from GitHub releases (or sudo apt install apktool)

tools.name: Bytecode Viewer
tools.desc: Swing viewer that combines dex2jar, CFR, and Procyon so one window shows decompiled Java plus raw bytecode for side-by-side review.
tools.when: Triage a stubborn APK when a single decompiler misses, and compare decompiler output in one place.
tools.install: Download the release jar from GitHub releases

tools.name: frida-dexdump
tools.desc: Dumps in-memory DEX files from a running app through Frida, defeating packers and protectors that only materialize code at runtime.
tools.when: Analyze a hardened or packed app: launch it on your test device, dump the loaded dex, then feed the recovered classes back into jadx.
tools.install: pip install frida-dexdump

tools.name: androguard
tools.desc: Python library plus CLI to parse DEX/APK graphs, list permissions and exported components, and script custom static checks.
tools.when: Scriptable static analysis and bespoke rules on apps you test when click-through GUI tools are not enough.
tools.install: pip install androguard

tools.name: Quark-Engine
tools.desc: Obfuscation-aware APK scoring engine that matches the app's call graph against suspicious-behavior rules (crypto misuse, dynamic dex loading, C2 calls) with confidence scores.
tools.when: Quick second opinion on an APK for risky behavior patterns after MobSF, or building your own detection rules from reversed code.
tools.install: pip3 install -U quark-engine && freshquark

tools.name: APKiD
tools.desc: YARA-based detector of packers, protectors, and obfuscators (DexProtector, Bangcle, qihoo) inside an APK or DEX before any reversing effort.
tools.when: Scope a hardened app early: knowing it is packed tells you static-only analysis is not enough and runtime dexdump is needed.
tools.install: pip install apkid

tools.name: mobsek
tools.desc: Offline mobile app security suite — APK/AXML/DEX, Mach-O, X.509 analysis, Frida hooks, deterministic threat score.
tools.when: Triage mobile apps you have permission to analyze.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/5h4d0wn1k/mobsek

tools.name: Frida (Android)
tools.desc: Injects frida-server onto a device to hook functions at runtime: bypass SSL pinning and root detection, trace crypto calls, and inspect memory.
tools.when: The runtime layer of most Android tests — bypass pinning, trace sensitive APIs, and probe internals static analysis cannot reach.
tools.install: pip install frida-tools && push a matching-version frida-server to the device

tools.name: objection
tools.desc: Frida-powered runtime exploration toolkit: one-liners to disable SSL pinning and root checks and browse storage (SharedPrefs, cache) without writing JS.
tools.when: Quick interactive runtime pass on your own app when hand-rolled Frida scripts are overkill.
tools.install: pip install objection

tools.name: drozer
tools.desc: On-device agent that assumes another app's identity to enumerate and test exported activities, content providers, services, and broadcast receivers from a console.
tools.when: After static analysis, map the app's IPC/component attack surface and probe each exported component for authorization and data-exposure flaws.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/ReversecLabs/drozer.git && cd drozer && pip install . (plus the drozer agent APK on the device)

tools.name: DIVA (Damn Insecure Vulnerable App)
tools.desc: Deliberately vulnerable Android app with a dozen fixed challenge categories (insecure logging, input validation, hardcoded keys) built for hands-on practice.
tools.when: Warming up static/dynamic skills or validating your toolchain before touching a real engagement target.
tools.install: Download the APK from GitHub releases and install it with adb install

tools.name: InsecureBankv2
tools.desc: Purposefully vulnerable banking app exposing auth bypass, SQL injection, and exposed adb port issues for controlled practice.
tools.when: Practicing mobile banking app tests (auth, crypto, IPC, storage) in an environment you fully control.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/dineshshetty/Android-InsecureBankv2 && run the bundled server, then install the APK via adb

tools.name: mitmproxy
tools.desc: Interactive HTTPS intercepting proxy built for mobile workflows: install its CA on the device, rewrite or replay HTTP/2 and gRPC, and script with Python addons.
tools.when: Any network-level test of your own apps — log, tamper, or replay API traffic from a rooted device or emulator, paired with a Frida pinning bypass.
tools.install: pip install mitmproxy

tools.name: Charles Proxy
tools.desc: Commercial GUI HTTPS proxy with click-through SSL proxying, breakpoints, and a request timeline — the macOS-centric alternative to a terminal proxy.
tools.when: Point-and-click interception and rewriting during manual iOS testing on a workstation when you prefer a GUI over mitmproxy.
tools.install: Download from charlesproxy.com (trial, then paid license)

tools.name: MobSF (Mobile Security Framework)
tools.desc: All-in-one analyzer for APK and IPA: permissions, exported components, insecure crypto and network config, hardcoded secrets, all surfaced in a web UI with a REST API; its dynamic module also captures app HTTP traffic.
tools.when: Always the first automated pass on a binary you are authorized to test — read the findings report, then drill into specific hits manually.
tools.install: docker run --rm -it -p 8000:8000 opensecurity/mobile-security-framework-mobsf:latest

tools.name: Genymotion
tools.desc: Fast x86 Android emulator with snapshots, sensor simulation, and drag-and-drop APK install — a convenient third-party run target for testing.
tools.when: When Android Studio's AVD is too heavy and you want quick snapshots and containerized test images for your own apps.
tools.install: Download the Genymotion bundle from genymotion.com (free personal-use desktop license)

tools.name: Waydroid
tools.desc: Container-based Android that boots a full Android userspace directly on Linux without a VM, scriptable from the CLI.
tools.when: Android testing on your Linux workstation with a container-native device instead of a heavyweight emulator.
tools.install: sudo apt install waydroid

tools.name: adb (Android Debug Bridge)
tools.desc: Google's core device bridge from Android platform-tools: install apps, push/pull files, shell in, install CA certificates, capture logcat, and port-forward.
tools.when: Every device setup step — reach the emulator or handset, push frida-server and test certificates, and snapshot app data before and after a run.
tools.install: sudo apt install adb

tools.name: Magisk
tools.desc: Systemless root with module support for dedicated test devices; gives Frida, adb, and injected agents the root context most dynamic tests need.
tools.when: Prepare a personal test device with an unlocked bootloader when an app refuses to run on stock or detects the emulator.
tools.install: Install the Magisk APK or fastboot boot a patched boot image on an unlocked-bootloader device

tools.name: LineageOS
tools.desc: The most widely used custom ROM: build or flash a controlled test image on your own device, enable adb root, and strip vendor bloat for cleaner testing.
tools.when: Standing up a long-lived controlled Android test device with root and current security patches before dynamic testing.
tools.install: Follow the device build instructions on wiki.lineageos.org and flash via adb/fastboot

tools.name: smali/baksmali
tools.desc: Assembler and disassembler for DEX bytecode: decode framework and system app code, patch small runtime checks, and reassemble for re-signing tests.
tools.when: Analyzing preinstalled or framework APKs on devices you own, or patching a specific smali check and rebuilding the APK.
tools.install: Download smali-2.x.jar and baksmali-2.x.jar from GitHub releases

tools.name: class-dump
tools.desc: Dumps Objective-C class interfaces from a Mach-O binary, exposing the app's object graph and method signatures for review.
tools.when: Mapping an app's Objective-C surface from a decrypted IPA you are authorized to test before deeper reversing.
tools.install: Download class-dump from the project page and place it in /usr/local/bin

tools.name: frida-ios-dump
tools.desc: Dumps the decrypted IPA from a jailbroken device using Frida, turning App Store-encrypted slices into analyzable binaries.
tools.when: Get a decryptable binary from your own jailbroken test device before starting static analysis.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/AloneMonkey/frida-ios-dump && cd frida-ios-dump && pip install -r requirements.txt && python3 dump.py <AppName>

tools.name: ipatool
tools.desc: Downloads IPAs directly from the App Store using your own Apple ID, enabling analysis of publicly available apps you lawfully retrieve.
tools.when: Pulling an IPA for review where you hold a valid Apple ID and authorization for the app.
tools.install: go install github.com/majd/ipatool/v2@latest

tools.name: Frida (iOS)
tools.desc: frida-server on a jailbroken device hooks and swizzles classes and traces methods for runtime inspection of your test apps.
tools.when: Tracing iOS app runtime behavior, bypassing cert pinning, and dumping decrypted classes on a device you control.
tools.install: Install frida-server via Sileo/Cydia and keep the version matched to the host pip install of frida-tools

tools.name: objection (iOS)
tools.desc: objection on iOS: disable SSL pinning, browse Keychain and UserDefaults, and explore classes from a single console without custom Frida JS.
tools.when: Fast runtime checks on your own jailbroken test device when writing Frida scripts is overkill.
tools.install: pip install objection

tools.name: cycript
tools.desc: Runtime REPL mixing Objective-C and JavaScript to poke live processes and objects on jailbroken devices.
tools.when: Interactive in-process class inspection and object manipulation during authorized iOS testing.
tools.install: Download the binary/dylib from cycript.org and launch with cycript -p <pid>

tools.name: Sileo
tools.desc: Modern package manager for jailbroken devices and the clean way to install frida-server, debuggers, and testing tweaks on your test device.
tools.when: Bootstrap a jailbroken lab device: install Frida, ldid, and testing utilities from one UI.
tools.install: Install Sileo from its GitHub release on a jailbroken device

tools.name: OWASP MASTG & UnCrackable Apps
tools.desc: The Mobile Security Testing Guide plus the UnCrackable APPv1-v4 challenge apps with documented solutions — the reference mobile CTF syllabus.
tools.when: Learning or validating a technique on trusted challenge apps before applying it to an authorized engagement.
tools.install: git clone https://github.com/OWASP/MASTG && run the UnCrackable APKs under Frida/objection on your test device

tools.name: DVIA (Damn Vulnerable iOS App)
tools.desc: Deliberately vulnerable iOS app for practicing jailbreak-based runtime testing around keychain, transport security, and privacy.
tools.when: Controlled iOS practice that mirrors real runtime vulnerabilities before touching your own production-grade apps.
tools.install: Build it from source in Xcode and deploy to a device you own

tools.name: Frida CodeShare
tools.desc: Community hub of reusable Frida scripts (pinning bypasses, trace templates, dexdump variants) for accelerating script authoring.
tools.when: Find a proven hooking pattern before writing your own custom script for an authorized app.
tools.install: Browse codeshare.frida.re and run a script with frida -l script.js
